B01_00: Surfactant protein C is produced by alveolar type II cells as a propeptide that must fold, traffic and be processed before joining the lipid film that prevents alveolar collapse. Mutations disrupting this cause misfolded pro-SFTPC to be retained, triggering ER stress, reactive oxygen species and autophagy that injure type II cells. Impaired surfactant homeostasis results, presenting as interstitial lung disease and neonatal respiratory distress.
B01_01: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase removes the sugar from inosine, guanosine and their deoxy forms, releasing bases for salvage. When defective, substrates accumulate and deoxyguanosine becomes dGTP, which inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and blocks DNA synthesis. T lymphocytes are most vulnerable, so deficiency causes profound T cell immunodeficiency with recurrent infection, often with neurological impairment and autoimmunity, paralleling adenosine deaminase deficiency.
B01_02: Ornithine transcarbamylase condenses ornithine with carbamoyl phosphate to form citrulline, the second urea cycle step in mitochondria. Amino acid substitutions cause ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency, the most common and only X-linked urea cycle disorder, with hyperammonaemia, encephalopathy, coma and neonatal death. Catalytic-site mutations abolish activity and present neonatally, while surface or interface changes cause later, stress-triggered disease, managed by nitrogen scavengers and protein restriction.
B01_03: Alveolar macrophages need GM-CSF signalling through a receptor of CSF2RA and CSF2RB subunits to clear surfactant. Loss-of-function CSF2RB mutations cause hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (surfactant metabolism dysfunction 5), where surfactant lipids and proteins secreted by type II cells are not taken up and degraded, filling alveoli and causing respiratory failure. The pathway links cytokine signalling to lung lipid homeostasis rather than surfactant synthesis.
B01_04: Isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase, a mitochondrial flavoenzyme in leucine catabolism, converts isovaleryl-CoA to 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA, and its loss causes isovaleric acidemia. Accumulated isovaleryl-CoA is diverted into isovaleric acid, glycine and carnitine conjugates, producing a sweaty-feet odour. Presentation ranges from neonatal crisis with acidosis, hyperammonaemia and seizures to mild intermittent disease, provoked by catabolic stress, and is managed with leucine restriction plus glycine and carnitine.
B01_05: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 catalyses the first, rate-limiting urea cycle step in liver mitochondria, forming carbamoyl phosphate from ammonia, bicarbonate and ATP. Recessive CPS1 variants cause hyperammonaemia, neonatal or stress-triggered, with cerebral oedema and neurological injury. The enzyme needs N-acetylglutamate activation; truncations upstream of its binding domain abolish activity, while missense changes in catalytic or channelling domains impair folding, and severity tracks residual activity.
B01_06: Adenosine deaminase converts adenosine and deoxyadenosine to inosine and deoxyinosine for purine disposal. When lost, deoxyadenosine accumulates and is phosphorylated to dATP, which blocks ribonucleotide reduction and DNA synthesis, especially in developing lymphocytes. The result is severe combined immunodeficiency with absent T, B and NK cells and skeletal, neurological and pulmonary features, treatable by enzyme replacement, transplantation or gene therapy.
B01_07: N-acetylglutamate synthase makes N-acetylglutamate from acetyl-CoA and glutamate in mitochondria, the obligatory activator of carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I that starts the urea cycle. Loss-of-function NAGS variants prevent carbamoyl phosphate formation, causing a rare recessive disorder with neonatal hyperammonaemia, vomiting, seizures, encephalopathy and low citrulline. Uniquely among urea cycle defects, it responds to carbamylglutamate, a stable activator analogue.
B01_08: The branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase complex commits leucine, isoleucine and valine to oxidation, and mutations disrupting its DBT-encoded E2 transacylase cause MSUD2. E2 carries lipoyl groups that accept acyl intermediates, so its loss stalls the complex despite intact E1. Branched-chain amino acids and ketoacids accumulate, causing sweet-smelling urine, encephalopathy, ketoacidosis and cerebral oedema, managed by dietary restriction.
B01_09: The mitochondrial branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase complex irreversibly decarboxylates branched-chain ketoacids, feeding the citric acid cycle; failure causes maple syrup urine disease with encephalopathy, ketoacidosis and sweet-smelling urine. Activity is switched off by E1 phosphorylation and restored by the phosphatase PPM1K. A PPM1K frameshift destabilises the phosphatase, locking the complex inactive and causing a mild variant corrected by restoring wild-type phosphatase.
B01_10: Dihydrolipoyl dehydrogenase is the shared E3 subunit of branched-chain ketoacid, alpha-ketoglutarate and pyruvate dehydrogenase complexes, reoxidising lipoamide and reducing NAD+. Recessive mutations disable all three, causing lactic acidosis, accumulation of pyruvate, branched-chain amino acids and alpha-keto acids, and neurological deterioration, sometimes with liver involvement. Classed with maple syrup urine disease, it differs biochemically, and residual activity predicts severity poorly.
B01_11: 3-Methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase, a biotin-dependent mitochondrial enzyme of leucine catabolism, converts 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA to 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA using MCCC1 (biotin-carrying) and MCCC2 (carboxyltransferase) subunits. Recessive mutations in either impair the enzyme, so intermediates spill into 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid and 3-methylcrotonylglycine. It is the commonest organic aciduria on newborn screening; most individuals are mild or asymptomatic, few have severe neonatal decompensation.
B01_12: Surfactant protein B, a hydrophobic peptide processed from a precursor in alveolar type II cells, spreads phospholipid films and lowers surface tension to prevent alveolar collapse. SFTPB mutations abolish it, causing abnormal lamellar bodies, incompletely processed SFTPC and accumulation of floccular material. The result is surfactant metabolism dysfunction type 1, a severe neonatal respiratory distress syndrome usually fatal without transplantation.
B01_13: Argininosuccinate lyase splits argininosuccinate into arginine and fumarate, the fourth urea cycle step that disposes of nitrogen and regenerates arginine. Recessive variants cause argininosuccinic aciduria, with neonatal hyperammonaemia, encephalopathy and respiratory alkalosis or milder stress-triggered disease. Intersubunit active sites allow allelic complementation and residual activity, and reduced arginine for nitric oxide synthesis may contribute to hypertension and neurological features.
B01_14: Alveolar macrophages require GM-CSF signalling, via a receptor of ligand-binding alpha and shared beta subunits, to mature and degrade surfactant. Loss-of-function alpha subunit mutations block this, so surfactant lipids and proteins A-D accumulate, causing hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (surfactant metabolism dysfunction type 4) with progressive hypoxaemic lung disease in children. Misfolded surfactant proproteins also provoke ER stress, oxidative stress and autophagy in alveolar epithelium.
B01_15: Ornithine transcarbamylase forms citrulline from carbamoyl phosphate and ornithine in mitochondria, the second urea cycle step, and is imported using a 33-residue N-terminal leader that is cleaved on arrival. Variants in this leader cause X-linked ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency by destabilising transcripts, lowering protein and preventing mitochondrial targeting. The result is hyperammonaemia with orotic aciduria and severe neonatal encephalopathy.
B01_16: Argininosuccinate synthase joins citrulline and aspartate into argininosuccinate using ATP, the third urea cycle step, mainly in hepatocyte cytosol, also supplying arginine for nitric oxide synthesis. Loss-of-function variants, including the recurrent G390R among over a hundred, cause type 1 citrullinaemia. Patients have hyperammonaemia with high citrulline, glutamine and orotic acid and low arginine, with severe neonatal lethargy, seizures, coma and death.
B01_17: ECHS1 is a mitochondrial hydratase acting in fatty acid beta-oxidation and branched-chain amino acid breakdown, preferring valine-derived methylacrylyl-CoA. Loss-of-function mutations cause short-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase deficiency, in which reactive acyl-CoA species accumulate and damage mitochondrial proteins. Patients develop Leigh-like encephalopathy with basal ganglia lesions, epilepsy, cardiac involvement and neurological regression, linking amino acid catabolism to brain energy supply.
B01_18: Adenine phosphoribosyltransferase salvages free adenine by transferring a phosphoribosyl group from PRPP to make AMP. When defective, adenine is oxidised by xanthine dehydrogenase to insoluble 2,8-dihydroxyadenine, which crystallises in urine and kidney. APRT deficiency therefore causes radiolucent kidney stones, crystalline nephropathy and renal failure that can recur after transplant unless xanthine oxidoreductase is inhibited, reflecting toxic accumulation rather than nucleotide shortage.
B01_19: SLC34A2 encodes NaPi-2b, an electrogenic sodium-phosphate cotransporter that lets alveolar type II cells recover phosphate from airspaces for surfactant synthesis, and also functions in intestinal and other epithelia. Loss of function leaves phosphate in alveolar fluid, where it precipitates as calcium phosphate microliths, causing pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis. Patients are often asymptomatic for years before slowly progressive decline in gas exchange and respiratory failure.
B01_20: The first committed step of branched-chain amino acid breakdown, oxidative decarboxylation of keto acids, is performed by the E1 heterotetramer of BCKDHA and BCKDHB on the DBT core. Severe mutations in either subunit disrupt assembly and abolish activity, causing classic maple syrup urine disease with sweet-smelling urine, neonatal encephalopathy, cerebral oedema and death if untreated. BCKDHA defines type 1A, BCKDHB type 1B.
B01_21: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase salvages hypoxanthine and guanine into IMP and GMP using PRPP. Without it, cells rely on costly de novo purine synthesis and unsalvaged bases are oxidised to urate. Partial deficiency causes gout and urate nephropathy, while near-complete deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan disease with hyperuricaemia, dystonia, cognitive impairment and self-injury, reflecting basal ganglia dependence on purine recycling.
B01_22: Branched-chain ketoacid dehydrogenase kinase phosphorylates the E1 alpha subunit to switch off irreversible branched-chain ketoacid degradation, sparing leucine, isoleucine and valine for protein synthesis. When the kinase is lost, the complex runs unrestrained and branched-chain amino acids fall in plasma and tissue. This mirror image of maple syrup urine disease causes intellectual disability, microcephaly and autistic features that respond to dietary supplementation.
B01_23: Beta-ketothiolase deficiency, or alpha-methylacetoacetic aciduria, results from loss of mitochondrial ACAT1, which cleaves 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA into propionyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA in isoleucine catabolism and also handles acetoacetyl-CoA in ketone utilisation. Isoleucine-derived organic acids accumulate diagnostically. Children usually present between six and eighteen months with infection- or fasting-triggered ketoacidotic crises, and management avoids catabolic stress.
B01_24: ABCA3 is a lipid transporter in alveolar type II cells that moves phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidylglycerol into lamellar bodies, where surfactant is packaged with its proteins to lower surface tension. When defective, lamellar bodies fail to mature and surfactant is deficient, causing surfactant metabolism dysfunction type 3. Severe cases cause fatal neonatal respiratory distress, milder ones chronic childhood interstitial lung disease.
B01_25: Cytosolic arginase 1, abundant in liver, hydrolyses arginine to urea and ornithine, completing the urea cycle. Recessive ARG1 variants cause hyperargininaemia, with arginine accumulating in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid. Unlike other urea cycle disorders, severe hyperammonaemia is uncommon; children develop progressive spastic paraparesis, developmental regression, seizures and growth failure, treated with protein restriction and nitrogen scavengers.
B01_26: Surfactant protein A2 is a collectin secreted by alveolar type II cells that organises surfactant lipids, regulates turnover and opsonises inhaled microbes. Folding mutations trap SFTPA2 in the endoplasmic reticulum, preventing secretion and imposing chronic unfolded protein stress on type II cells. This causes familial idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, with repeated epithelial injury, progressive scarring and fatal respiratory failure within years.
B01_27: HIBCH hydrolyses 3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA to 3-hydroxyisobutyrate and CoA, the fifth step of mitochondrial valine catabolism. In recessive HIBCH deficiency, the reactive acyl-CoA accumulates and, as in ECHS1 deficiency, modifies protein cysteines including those of pyruvate dehydrogenase. The result is Leigh-like encephalopathy with psychomotor regression, developmental delay, neurodegeneration and symmetrical basal ganglia lesions.
B01_28: The mitochondrial hydratase AUH converts 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA to HMG-CoA, the fifth step of leucine catabolism feeding ketone body and acetyl-CoA production. Recessive loss-of-function mutations cause 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, with 3-methylglutaconic, 3-methylglutaric and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acids accumulating in urine. Severity ranges from incidental finding to acidosis, encephalopathy and coma, depending on residual activity and tissue reliance on leucine oxidation.
B01_29: SLC25A15 exchanges cytosolic ornithine for mitochondrial citrulline across the inner membrane, linking the urea cycle's two compartments. Loss-of-function variants cause hyperornithinaemia-hyperammonaemia-homocitrullinuria syndrome: matrix ornithine shortage leads carbamoyl phosphate to react with lysine, forming homocitrulline, and ammonia rises. Patients have episodic encephalopathy, protein intolerance, spastic paraparesis and developmental impairment, partly buffered by SLC25A2.
